summary: OneCLI is a team platform for hosted agents, not a standalone coding CLI. The only in-repo agent runtime is apps/sandbox-supervisor (@onecli/sandbox-supervisor), a Node 22 program that runs inside each agent sandbox: it renders instruction files (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md) into the agent home, spawns the pinned third-party jcode v0.81.1 runtime (a Rust binary vendored from GitHub releases, driven via @1jehuang/jcode-sdk over a unix socket), and speaks a vendor-neutral transport. With no RUNNER_WS_URL it uses the stdio transport: JSONL work items on stdin ({"kind":"turn.deliver",...} then {"kind":"shutdown"}) and JSONL events/turn.result on stdout, logs on stderr. The bundled entrypoint is dist/index.mjs (built with esbuild via `pnpm --filter @onecli/sandbox-supervisor build`). Model calls are made by jcode itself: with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set it uses its native Claude provider and POSTs streaming requests with tool definitions to `${ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL}/messages` (x-api-key auth), so ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL must be `$PROXY_URL/v1`. The model is chosen by AGENT_MODEL (passed through to jcode's setModel). The previous failure (aarch64 jcode needs GLIBC 2.38/2.39 + libssl3, absent on bookworm 2.36 and jammy 2.35) is fixed by bundling Ubuntu noble's libc6/libgcc-s1/libssl3t64 under /opt/harness/sysroot and re-pointing the binary's ELF interpreter and rpath there with a static patchelf; the x86_64 release needs only GLIBC 2.17 and is left untouched. Verified: builds + check command pass on arm64 python:3.12-slim-bookworm, arm64 buildpack-deps:jammy and emulated amd64 buildpack-deps:jammy; a full turn with a tool call completed against a mock Anthropic Messages server on both arm64 images.
dockerfile:
ARG BASE=python:3.12-slim-bookworm
FROM ${BASE}

# OneCLI overlay: the in-sandbox supervisor (apps/sandbox-supervisor) driving the
# pinned jcode runtime, self-contained under /opt/harness. Nothing from the base
# image's python/node is used or changed.
ARG TARGETARCH
ARG NODE_VERSION=22.23.2
ARG PNPM_VERSION=9.0.0
ARG JCODE_VERSION=v0.81.1
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
      ca-certificates curl git ripgrep procps \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Node runtime (official tarball, checksum-verified) -> /opt/harness/node
RUN set -eu; \
    ARCH="${TARGETARCH:-$(dpkg --print-architecture)}"; \
    case "$ARCH" in \
      amd64) NODE_ARCH=x64;   NODE_SHA=b294a556e639d64338823920e5866c21c02741742d2e1529ee1a225c1ec9252a ;; \
      arm64) NODE_ARCH=arm64; NODE_SHA=013b59cfd2819703a6f4a14ab891fc46fc2a4e3f5bcd92de3fb4929b43e35b30 ;; \
      *) echo "unsupported arch: $ARCH" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
    esac; \
    mkdir -p /opt/harness/node /opt/harness/bin; \
    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/node.tar.gz "https://nodejs.org/dist/v${NODE_VERSION}/node-v${NODE_VERSION}-linux-${NODE_ARCH}.tar.gz"; \
    echo "${NODE_SHA}  /tmp/node.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -; \
    tar -xzf /tmp/node.tar.gz -C /opt/harness/node --strip-components=1; \
    rm -f /tmp/node.tar.gz
ENV PATH=/opt/harness/bin:/opt/harness/node/bin:$PATH
# Login shells (`bash -lc`) get PATH reset by /etc/profile; re-add ours there.
RUN printf 'export PATH=/opt/harness/bin:/opt/harness/node/bin:$PATH\n' > /etc/profile.d/onecli-harness.sh
RUN npm install -g "pnpm@${PNPM_VERSION}" && npm cache clean --force

# The pinned jcode runtime (same release + checksums as docker/agent.Dockerfile).
# x86_64 ships a launcher script + .bin (needs only GLIBC 2.17); aarch64 ships a
# bare ELF that needs GLIBC 2.39 + libssl3, which bookworm (2.36) and jammy
# (2.35) lack. For arm64 we bundle Ubuntu noble's glibc/libgcc/libssl under
# /opt/harness/sysroot (checksum-verified debs, unpacked with dpkg-deb, no
# packages touched) and point the binary's interpreter/rpath at them with a
# static patchelf that is used once and removed.
RUN set -eu; \
    ARCH="${TARGETARCH:-$(dpkg --print-architecture)}"; \
    case "$ARCH" in \
      amd64) ASSET=jcode-linux-x86_64;  SHA=ddfd6b8f7d6fe15284d78785eda1130a6e2ecd8d3352f20628822a1eb7aa2549 ;; \
      arm64) ASSET=jcode-linux-aarch64; SHA=89712dd36de31905a23850f4af0af18081bcf26088c7c359c53d9dbdec897919 ;; \
      *) echo "unsupported arch: $ARCH" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
    esac; \
    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/jcode.tar.gz "https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode/releases/download/${JCODE_VERSION}/${ASSET}.tar.gz"; \
    echo "${SHA}  /tmp/jcode.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -; \
    mkdir -p /opt/harness/jcode; \
    tar -xzf /tmp/jcode.tar.gz -C /opt/harness/jcode; \
    mv "/opt/harness/jcode/${ASSET}" /opt/harness/jcode/jcode; \
    chmod 0755 /opt/harness/jcode/*; \
    rm -f /tmp/jcode.tar.gz; \
    if [ "$ARCH" = arm64 ]; then \
      SR=/opt/harness/sysroot; LIBDIR="$SR/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu"; \
      mkdir -p "$SR" /tmp/debs; \
      POOL=http://ports.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-ports/pool/main; \
      for spec in \
        "g/glibc/libc6_2.39-0ubuntu8_arm64.deb 04d7cb73e608b41713b63ef915577f7f5d75e95b1b33174e82e05687fdb6cfaf" \
        "g/gcc-14/libgcc-s1_14-20240412-0ubuntu1_arm64.deb bb1c262f2ac9aeb357d3344a06f22f1057306694f6200896775a03ecced08b13" \
        "o/openssl/libssl3t64_3.0.13-0ubuntu3_arm64.deb d2207f12435060893997880a34d7ed91d14e163862d5d1394d51918d0723d7e0"; \
      do \
        set -- $spec; f="/tmp/debs/$(basename "$1")"; \
        curl -fsSL -o "$f" "$POOL/$1"; \
        echo "$2  $f" | sha256sum -c -; \
        dpkg-deb -x "$f" "$SR"; \
      done; \
      rm -rf /tmp/debs; \
      test -x "$LIBDIR/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1"; \
      test -e "$LIBDIR/libc.so.6" && test -e "$LIBDIR/libssl.so.3" && test -e "$LIBDIR/libgcc_s.so.1"; \
      curl -fsSL -o /tmp/patchelf.tar.gz https://github.com/NixOS/patchelf/releases/download/0.18.0/patchelf-0.18.0-aarch64.tar.gz; \
      echo "ae13e2effe077e829be759182396b931d8f85cfb9cfe9d49385516ea367ef7b2  /tmp/patchelf.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -; \
      mkdir -p /tmp/patchelf && tar -xzf /tmp/patchelf.tar.gz -C /tmp/patchelf; \
      /tmp/patchelf/bin/patchelf --set-interpreter "$LIBDIR/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1" \
        --force-rpath --set-rpath "$LIBDIR" /opt/harness/jcode/jcode; \
      rm -rf /tmp/patchelf /tmp/patchelf.tar.gz; \
    fi; \
    JCODE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 JCODE_NO_TELEMETRY=1 /opt/harness/jcode/jcode --version | grep -F "jcode ${JCODE_VERSION} "
ENV ONECLI_JCODE_BINARY=/opt/harness/jcode/jcode

# The harness source, installed and bundled in place (pnpm workspace subset)
COPY . /opt/harness/src
RUN cd /opt/harness/src \
 && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts --store-dir /opt/harness/.pnpm-store \
      --filter "@onecli/sandbox-supervisor..." \
 && pnpm --filter @onecli/sandbox-supervisor build \
 && rm -rf /opt/harness/.pnpm-store \
 && test -f /opt/harness/src/apps/sandbox-supervisor/dist/index.mjs \
 && test -f /opt/harness/src/apps/sandbox-supervisor/dist/mcp-bridge/bridge.mjs

# Entrypoint shim: the supervisor's own CLI (JSONL work items on stdin)
RUN printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec node /opt/harness/src/apps/sandbox-supervisor/dist/index.mjs "$@"\n' \
      > /opt/harness/bin/onecli-supervisor \
 && chmod 0755 /opt/harness/bin/onecli-supervisor

ENV JCODE_NO_TELEMETRY=1 \
    JCODE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 \
    NO_COLOR=1
run_command:
export PATH=/opt/harness/bin:/opt/harness/node/bin:$PATH
set -o pipefail
export AGENT_HOME_DIR="$PWD"
export AGENT_NAME="${AGENT_NAME:-onecli-agent}"
mkdir -p /out
KEEP="$(mktemp -d)"
for f in AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md; do [ -e "$f" ] && cp -p "$f" "$KEEP/$f"; done
if [ -z "${AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS:-}" ]; then AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS="$(cat "$KEEP"/AGENTS.md "$KEEP"/CLAUDE.md 2>/dev/null)"; export AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS; fi
had_jh=0; [ -e .jcode-home ] && had_jh=1
had_ag=0; [ -e .agents ] && had_ag=1
had_pj=0; [ -e .jcode ] && had_pj=1
node -e 'process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({kind:"turn.deliver",turnId:"task-1",conversationId:"task",message:process.env.TASK})+"\n"+JSON.stringify({kind:"shutdown"})+"\n")' \
  | onecli-supervisor > >(tee /out/trajectory.jsonl) 2> >(tee /out/supervisor.log >&2)
rc=$?
for f in AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md; do rm -f "$f"; [ -e "$KEEP/$f" ] && cp -p "$KEEP/$f" "$f"; done
rm -rf "$KEEP"
[ -d .jcode-home ] && cp -r .jcode-home /out/jcode-home 2>/dev/null
[ "$had_jh" = 1 ] || rm -rf .jcode-home
[ "$had_ag" = 1 ] || rm -rf .agents
[ "$had_pj" = 1 ] || rm -rf .jcode
node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const r=fs.readFileSync("/out/trajectory.jsonl","utf8").split("\n").map(s=>{try{return JSON.parse(s)}catch{return null}}).filter(m=>m&&m.kind==="turn.result").pop();if(!r){console.error("no turn.result (supervisor rc '"$rc"')");process.exit(2)}console.error("turn "+r.status+(r.error?": "+r.error:""));process.exit(r.status==="done"?0:1)'
check_command: export PATH=/opt/harness/bin:/opt/harness/node/bin:$PATH; "$ONECLI_JCODE_BINARY" --version && node --version && d="$(mktemp -d)" && out="$(printf '{"kind":"shutdown"}\n' | AGENT_HARNESS=fake AGENT_HOME_DIR="$d" onecli-supervisor 2>/dev/null)" && echo "$out" | grep -q '"kind":"ready"' && echo "onecli supervisor OK"
notes: What failed before: the evaluator builds on an arm64 host, and the aarch64 jcode v0.81.1 release is a bare ELF that NEEDs libssl.so.3/libcrypto.so.3/libgcc_s.so.1 and GLIBC up to 2.39, so it cannot load on python:3.12-slim-bookworm (glibc 2.36) or buildpack-deps:jammy arm64 (glibc 2.35). Fix: on arm64 the Dockerfile downloads Ubuntu noble's libc6 2.39-0ubuntu8, libgcc-s1 14-20240412-0ubuntu1 and libssl3t64 3.0.13-0ubuntu3 arm64 debs (release-pocket URLs on ports.ubuntu.com, sha256 pinned), unpacks them with dpkg-deb into /opt/harness/sysroot without touching base packages, then uses the static patchelf 0.18.0 tarball (sha256 pinned, deleted afterwards) to set the binary's interpreter to the sysroot ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 and its DT_RPATH to the sysroot libdir. A plain `ld.so --library-path` wrapper was rejected because jcode calls current_exe(). The build then gates on `jcode --version` matching the pin. amd64 is unchanged (x86_64 release needs only GLIBC 2.17 and no libssl; the `openssl` apt package was dropped as unneeded). Verified with Docker on this arm64 host: builds + check_command (via bash -lc) pass on arm64 python:3.12-slim-bookworm, arm64 buildpack-deps:jammy and emulated amd64 buildpack-deps:jammy; a full turn against a mock Anthropic Messages server on both arm64 images ran jcode's `write` tool in the task cwd, streamed the answer, and ended with turn.result status "done" (run exit 0), with the repo's AGENTS.md restored afterwards. Other gotchas (unchanged): jcode appends `/messages` to ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, hence `$PROXY_URL/v1`; `bash -lc` resets PATH via /etc/profile, so /etc/profile.d/onecli-harness.sh re-adds it and both commands export PATH. The supervisor renders its own instruction doc over AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md (0444) in the home dir and creates .jcode-home/.agents/.jcode; the run command feeds pre-existing AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md in as AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS, restores them afterwards, copies jcode session state to /out/jcode-home, and removes created scaffolding. Platform tools (memory, schedules, processes, Slack) go over an MCP bridge whose RPCs expect a runner and time out (~25s) on stdio if the model calls them; jcode's native file/bash tools are unaffected. Outputs: /out/trajectory.jsonl (supervisor JSONL events), /out/supervisor.log. Optional AGENT_EFFORT=low|medium|high|max.
